rules: Use ?number=XXXX to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
Do NOT use other query params — they are not supported.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
POSTING BALANCE RULES (which determines single-leg vs manual-leg):
vatType != 0 (e.g. id=3 for 25%): include ONLY the debit posting with GROSS amount. Tripletex auto-generates VAT + credit.
vatType == 0 (exempt): include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': you used vatType=0 but only one posting. Either add the credit posting manually OR change to the correct vatType (e.g. 3 for 25%).
NEVER default to vatType=0 for standard purchases — use vatType=3 (25%) unless explicitly VAT-exempt.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For salary/payroll vouchers, set employee={"id": employee_id} on each posting.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}.

payload.headline: All 5 checks failed: wrong expense account (6540 vs expected) and likely wrong VAT/posting structure
what_went_wrong: Used account 6540 (Inventar/fixed assets) for a USB hub instead of the correct expense account (likely 6800 or similar office/IT supplies account), causing all checks to fail.
Two 422 errors wasted calls trying vatType id=1 and id=3 for auto-generation before falling back to manual postings — the auto-generation approach was never going to work without a credit posting.

Manual posting approach with vatType=0 and separate 2710 VAT line may not match what the scorer expects — the scorer likely expects a specific vatType on the expense line rather than manual VAT splitting.
Multiple redundant GET /ledger/account calls (4 total) to resolve accounts 2710, 2920, 2400, and 2916 could have been batched or known in advance, adding unnecessary overhead.
what_worked: Department 'Lager' and supplier 'Komplett' were created successfully with correct data.
The gross amount (14,550), net (11,640), and VAT (2,910) calculations were mathematically correct.
what_to_try_next: Use a standard office/IT supplies expense account (e.g., 6800 Kontorrekvisita or 6860 Rekvisita) instead of 6540 (Inventar) — a USB hub is a consumable, not a fixed asset.
Try using the supplier invoice endpoint (/supplier/invoice) instead of /ledger/voucher, which may handle VAT auto-splitting correctly and match the scorer's expectations.
Pre-resolve common account numbers (2710, 2400) from the initial GET /ledger/account call instead of making 4 separate account lookup calls to reduce total API calls.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account for account 2920 — not needed since company card payment should use 2400 or similar, not 2920
GET /ledger/account for account 2916 — this account doesn't exist, wasted call
POST /ledger/voucher with vatType id=1 — first failed attempt before trying id=3, both were predictably wrong
